name: Presscart
description: Media marketplace for founders/marketers/agencies to buy press placements that rank in Google and show up in AI answers — article + interview + backlink packs (promo ~$599, normally ~$999). Y Combinator–backed. Founded Mar 2016, US. ~2,000 estimated users.

mentions.evidence: ~$2,000 MRR, 2 active subscriptions, ~$62,199 L30, ~$3,265,158 all-time. Caveat: Stripe API key expired Jul 17, 2026; treat L30/MRR as last-synced cache (profile refresh around that date).
mentions.indieAngle: Marketplace one boring media outcome (guest posts in one niche, podcast bookings, local newspaper placements) with fixed SKUs. Charge per placement, not seats.

whyItPrints: Marketplace take-rate on PR inventory. Tiny seat MRR (~$2k / 2 subs) but ~$62k L30 and ~$3.3M all-time from transactional placements. "Skip the agency retainer, buy the placement" — unsexy media ops glue.
whyThisMatters:
Founders, marketers, and agencies buy one press placement at a time. You pick a publisher from a catalog they say holds more than 1,700 sites. The price, the rules, and the turnaround sit on the listing before you pay. When it runs, you get a live URL.

The piece can be a founder profile, a product story, or a comment from an expert. You answer a short set of questions. Human editors write it to that publication's rules. What they're selling is a page that can turn up in Google and in AI answers, and each placement is labeled as a placement.

The company started in the US in March 2016 and is backed by Y Combinator. The checkout is that article and that link.

Founders buy press placements as a product, not a retainer.
